subject.title: fix(marketplaces): allow trusted feed key rotation

question: After a signing key is revoked or an emergency replacement root is deployed, should monotonic metadata authenticated under the former key continue to reject lower-sequence feeds, and what supported recovery path should reset that retained authority?
rationale: The code correctly preserves rollback protection across ordinary rotation, but the acceptable availability-versus-revocation tradeoff is a product security contract that source inspection cannot choose safely.

options.title: Specify revoked-key recovery before merge
options.body: Document and test the supported reset or Doctor recovery path for a newly trusted feed whose sequence is below retained signed metadata.

options.title: Accept durable rollback authority
options.body: Approve the current behavior as intentional: previously authenticated metadata remains rejection-only authority across key replacement, even if recovery requires external sequence continuity.

options.title: Require current-trust revalidation
options.body: Retain the prior requirement that an old snapshot validate under current keys, accepting that ordinary key rotation needs another rollback-protection design.

recommendation.title: Specify revoked-key recovery before merge
recommendation.body: Document and test the supported reset or Doctor recovery path for a newly trusted feed whose sequence is below retained signed metadata.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest visible context for the linked signed-feed trust direction, although the final security-policy decision requires a repository owner.
